body.p: The Applicant has considered the Office action dated July 21, 2023, and the references cited therein. By way of this response, claims 1, 11, and 18 have been amended. Claim 6 has been cancelled without prejudice to its further prosecution. New claim 21 has been added. All claims are supported by the specification. No new matter has been added. This application is in condition for allowance and favorable reconsideration is respectfully requested.

The Rejections Under 35 U.S.C. § 102 and § 103 Claims 1, 11, 18, and 19 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as allegedly anticipated by Landers et al., European Patent Application Publication No. EP3907136. Claims 2-10, 12, 13, 15, 16, and 20 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Landers et al. in view of Rambo, U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2022/0243667. Claim 14 stands rejected under § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Landers et al. in view of Rambo and Lavoie et al., European Patent Application No. EP3578464. Claim 17 stands rejected under § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Landers et al. in view of Rambo and Mariotto et al., European Patent Application No. EP3805107. The Applicant traverses all of the reference-based rejections.1

Claim 1: Independent claim 1 sets forth a hybrid-electric powertrain including a clutch between a generator and a drive shaft. In claim 1, the generator is disconnected from the drive shaft during a second mode of operation via the clutch. In claim 1, during the second mode of

1 The Applicant notes that claims 6, 7, 9, 10 depend from claim 1. Claim 1 stands rejected under § 102 as allegedly anticipated by Landers et al. However, with respect to claims 6, 7, 9, 10, the Office action states that "Landers and Rambo teach the limitations set forth in claim 1." See present Office action, p. 7-8. Similarly, claims 14 and 16 depend from claim 11 and claim 11 stands rejected under § 102 as allegedly anticipated by Landers et al. However, with respect to claims 14 and 16, the Office action states that "Landers and Rambo teach the limitations set forth in claim 11." See id. at pp. 9, 11. The Applicant respectfully requests clarification of the record to indicate that independent claims 1 and 11 have only been rejected under § 102 with respect to Landers et al. and have not been rejected based on Rambo.

operation, a gas turbine propulsion engine is activated to produce thrust and an electric propulsion unit is deactivated. None of the cited references teaches or suggests such a hybrid- electric powertrain.
The Office action admits that Landers et al. do not teach or suggest a clutch between a

Landers et al. mention that "[i]n response to disengaging the electric engine, the aircraft may then be propelled only by the turbine engine or other combustion engine." See Landers et al., para. [0025]. Landers et al. mention that "[t]he method may next be operative to charge 360 a battery used to power the electric engine. The battery may be charged by a generator powered by the turbine." Id. Thus, Landers et al. expressly mention that when an electric engine is disengaged, a generator powered by a turbine may be used to charge a battery. Therefore, contrary to the arguments in the Office action, it would not be obvious to one or ordinary skill in the art to modify Landers et al. to disconnect a generator from a drive shaft of a gas turbine engine during a second mode of operation as set forth in claim 1. Rather, Landers et al. mention using a generator powered by a turbine to charge a battery while an electric engine is disengaged (e.g., during a second mode of operation). Accordingly, Landers et al. do not teach or suggest a
clutch between a generator and a drive shaft, the generator disconnected from the drive shaft during a second mode of operation via the clutch, as set forth in claim 1.
The Office action also admits that Rambo does not teach or suggest a clutch between a

generator and a drive shaft to disconnect the generator from the drive shaft during a second mode of operation. See present Office action, p. 7. Further, neither Lavoie et al. nor Mariotto et al. teaches or suggests a clutch between a generator and a drive shaft, the generator disconnected from the drive shaft during a second mode of operation via the clutch, as set forth in claim 1. Thus, none of Rambo, Lavoie et al., or Mariotto et al. cures the deficiencies of Lander et al.

Accordingly, none of Landers et al., Rambo, Lavoie et al. or Mariotto et al., alone or in combination, teaches or suggests the hybrid-electric powertrain of claim 1. Withdrawal of the reference-based rejections of claim 1 and all claims depending therefrom is respectfully requested.
Claim 11: Independent claim 11 sets forth an aircraft including a hybrid electric

powertrain. In claim 11, the hybrid electric powertrain includes means for disconnecting a generator from gas turbine engine during a second mode of operation. None of Landers et al., Rambo, Lavoie et al. or Mariotto et al., alone or in combination, teaches or suggests an aircraft. Withdrawal of the reference-based rejections of claim 11 and all claims depending therefrom is respectfully requested.

Claim 18: Independent claim 18 sets forth a method including decoupling a generator from a gas turbine propulsion engine during a second segment of flight via a clutch. None of Landers et al., Rambo, Lavoie et al. or Mariotto et al., alone or in combination, teaches or suggests a method. Withdrawal of the reference-based rejections of claim 18 and all claims depending therefrom is respectfully requested.

In general, the Office makes various statements regarding the pending claims that are now moot in light of the above. Thus, the Applicant will not address such statements at the present time. However, the Applicant expressly reserves the right to challenge such statements in the future should the need arise (e.g., if such statement should become relevant by appearing in a rejection of any current or future claim).
